svg.title: Frontal evolution, cortical layers, and circuit organization
svg.desc: Three-panel schematic. A: lateral and medial views of mouse and macaque cerebral hemispheres, rostral to the left. Selected medial frontal areas are shaded ochre on the medial surface in both species. In the macaque lateral view, a broad granular lateral prefrontal field is shaded blue rostral to the arcuate sulcus, with motor and premotor cortex hatched in neutral gray between the arcuate and central sulci; the mouse lateral view has no comparable field. Not to scale. B: three equal-height schematic strips of primate frontal cortex, pial surface at top and white matter below, labeled agranular, dysgranular and granular. The granular strip has a distinct layer IV band of densely packed small cell bodies, tinted blue, labeled with layers I to VI. The dysgranular strip has a thin, irregular, faint layer IV. The agranular strip shows a continuous cell distribution from layer III into layer V with no separate layer IV. Thin magnification lines connect the granular strip to panel C. C: enlarged patch of granular macaque lateral prefrontal cortex. A teal axon from the mediodorsal (MD) thalamus ascends through white matter and branches in deep layer III and layer IV near small excitatory neurons. One of these exchanges connections with a layer II/III pyramidal neuron. Three layer II/III pyramidal neurons excite one another reciprocally; one of them excites an inhibitory interneuron, which inhibits pyramidal neurons (T-bars). A layer II/III pyramidal axon leaves through white matter to other association cortex, and a separate return axon re-enters to terminate in middle and deep layer III. A layer VI neuron sends a separate axon back to MD thalamus.
